responsibilities.name: Nightly Regression Suite
responsibilities.instruction: Run the saved regression test suite, diff results against the last baseline, and write a regression report to MEMORY.md.

context.purpose: Catch regressions early by running the full test suite every night and comparing results to the last known-good baseline. Provides a daily quality signal.
process: STEP 1 — Load the regression suite definition from the project's test configuration or MEMORY.md test registry.
STEP 2 — Execute all tests in the suite. Do NOT skip any tests without a documented reason.
STEP 3 — Collect structured results: {pass, fail, skip, error} counts and failure details with evidence.
STEP 4 — Load the last baseline results from MEMORY.md or the test results archive.
STEP 5 — Compute the regression diff: new failures, fixes, persistent failures, new tests.
STEP 6 — Flag any unexplained skips or test count anomalies.
STEP 7 — Write the regression report to MEMORY.md under '## Latest Regression Run'.
STEP 8 — If any S1/S2 regressions are found, escalate immediately to the operator.
STEP 9 — Save current results as the new baseline for tomorrow's comparison.
context.success_criteria: Regression report written with pass/fail/skip counts, regression diff against baseline, all failures have evidence, and S1/S2 regressions escalated.
context.prior_learnings: Flaky tests can create false regression signals — track flaky history and note it in the diff. Always check that total test count is consistent with baseline; a drop may indicate tests were removed rather than fixed.

responsibilities.name: Weekly Defect Aging Review
responsibilities.instruction: Review all open defects, flag stale items that have not been updated in >7 days, reassess severity based on current context, and update the defect tracking sheet.

context.purpose: Prevent defects from going stale and ensure severity ratings reflect current reality. Keeps the defect backlog honest and actionable.
process: STEP 1 — Load the current defect list from the tracking sheet or MEMORY.md defect registry.
STEP 2 — For each open defect, check the last update date.
STEP 3 — Flag any defect with no update in >7 days as STALE.
STEP 4 — Reassess severity for stale defects: has the impact changed? Is the workaround still valid? Has the affected feature been deprecated?
STEP 5 — Update severity if warranted (document the reason for any change).
STEP 6 — Produce an aging summary: total open, stale count, severity distribution (S1/S2/S3/S4), oldest open defect.
STEP 7 — Write the aging report to MEMORY.md under '## Defect Aging Report'.
STEP 8 — If any S1 defects are >48 hours old without progress, escalate to the operator.
context.success_criteria: Aging report written with stale defect count, severity distribution, and any re-severity justifications. S1 defects >48h escalated.
context.prior_learnings: Severity drift is real — a defect filed as S3 may become S2 if the workaround breaks or if the feature becomes more critical. Always re-evaluate in current context rather than rubber-stamping the original severity.
